data.question: What primary City record advances #1951's named Syracuse Axon control chain without confusing municipal governance roles with platform administrator credentials?
data.method: Deduped the current Syracuse transition corpus, then reconciled the City of Syracuse February 10, 2026 STWG presentation with the existing January 27 procurement baseline.
data.framework: Keep public-official governance/approval roles separate from native vendor-platform roles, credentials, configuration changes, audit events, and Flock-to-Axon migration.
data.scope: Syracuse Axon ALPR committee review and Common Council approval chain, February 6-10, 2026.
findings: At the February 6 joint Public Safety & Economic Development committee meeting, Corporation Counsel Sue Katzoff and SPD Deputy Chief Trudell answered council questions about the Axon cameras, data collection, and sharing.
On February 9 Common Council passed revocable right-of-way permission for Axon to construct, own, operate, and maintain the citywide LPR deployment under a Police Department MSA.
The council also passed the 26-reader purchase/install/maintenance agreement effective March 1 for 60 months, with the first 12 months free and a $422,636.28 not-to-exceed amount.
The City presentation records that the Commissioner of Finance would determine the funding account and that the Mayor waived the RFP process.
These facts establish municipal review/approval responsibilities, not native Axon account ownership or configuration actions.
conclusions: The public Axon approval chain is now better anchored to a primary City record with named legal and police participants plus council, mayoral, and finance roles.

#1951's higher-value control question remains open because public governance participation is not evidence of native platform administrator credentials, actual configuration changes, or audit-log events.
recommendations: Recover the executed Axon MSA and all schedules/order forms, including named signatories and support/admin provisions.
Recover native Axon user/admin/role, retention, sharing, audit, hotlist and case-number configuration exports.
Recover Flock Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks, user/admin, credential-revocation and deletion/retention closeout records.
Only add actor-to-platform-control edges where native records identify the account, role, action, timestamp and authorization.
counterarguments: Committee participation can show policy responsibility but cannot safely be promoted into a technical administrator relation without platform-native evidence.
limitations: This pass advances the public governance/control chain only; it does not complete the national-sharing incident reconstruction, Flock offboarding, Axon control matrix, or migration findings.
unresolved: Who held Flock and Axon administrator accounts and during what effective dates?
Which account enabled national sharing and who authorized it?
What native records document rollback, credential revocation, and deletion/retention closeout?
Who signed and administered the executed Axon MSA?
What native Axon audit records tie named actors to actual platform actions?
